title: A network partition: what a CP system and an AP system do with a write
captions: Two replicas, A and B, hold the stock count for one item. There is 1 left. A copies every change to B, so they agree.
The network link between A and B breaks. Both replicas are still running. They just cannot talk to each other. This is a network partition.
Ravi's app is connected to B. He taps Buy on the last item. B must choose now: answer him, or stay correct.
A CP system says no. B cannot check with A, so it returns an error. The data stays correct, but Ravi cannot buy for now.
An AP system says yes. B sells the item to Ravi. On the other side, A has sold the same item to Asha. Both got an answer, but one item was sold twice.
The link comes back. In the CP system, B catches up with A and nothing needs fixing. The AP system must merge the two histories and fix the conflict, for example by cancelling one order.
